odunpazarievleri.name: Odunpazarı Houses
odunpazarievleri.slogan: Overhanging timber upper floors on cobbled lanes.
odunpazarievleri.line: Odunpazarı means "firewood market" in Turkish, and the quarter is on Turkey's tentative UNESCO World Heritage list.

midasanitiyazilikaya.name: Midas Monument
midasanitiyazilikaya.slogan: A Phrygian palace front carved into living rock.
midasanitiyazilikaya.line: The cliff facade carries an Old Phrygian dedication to Midas, naming him with the title for ruler, and dates to the 7th century BC.

odunpazarimodern.name: Odunpazarı Modern Museum
odunpazarimodern.slogan: Stacked timber boxes echoing the old houses around them.
odunpazarimodern.line: Designed by Kengo Kuma and Associates, the museum opened in 2019 and takes its name from the old firewood-market district.

battalgazi.name: Seyyid Battal Gazi Complex
battalgazi.slogan: A hillside shrine where legend and pilgrims meet.
battalgazi.line: The tomb beside the Seyitgazi complex was restored in 1464, and the mosque rebuilt in 1511; the site was also a major Bektashi lodge.

ertugrulturbesi.name: Ertuğrul Gazi Tomb
ertugrulturbesi.slogan: Where the Ottoman story begins, in the hills of Söğüt.
ertugrulturbesi.line: The present mausoleum at Söğüt was built under Sultan Abdulhamid II (r. 1876-1909); the early Ottoman tomb was rebuilt repeatedly.
